text: Stand on a beach, and look out to sea.
How far away is the horizon?
Blue is what we know. Red is what we want.
Your line of sight just grazes the Earth, at a right angle.
Aitch squared is tiny, so we drop it.
asr: H squared is tiny, so we drop it.

text: From one point six metres up: about four and a half kilometres.
Now, climb a hundred times higher.
You see only ten times farther.
From a plane, ten kilometres up: about three hundred and fifty-seven kilometres.
asr: From a plane, 10 kilometers up, about 357 kilometers.

text: The view grows only with the square root of your height.
